definition: For an already-active company×track pair, the pair's historical 12-month FDA activity rate predicts whether at least one material public Traditional 510(k) or original/panel-track PMA event occurs in the next 12 months.
sample_scope: reverse_rd_v1: 6,701 matured pair-origin examples, 3,833 material events, 51 companies, 322 pairs. Final three untouched holdout origins: 2025-04-01, 2025-07-01, 2025-10-01 (302/307/307 rows).
information_cutoff: Quarterly rolling origins from 2019-10-01 through 2025-10-01; features require available_at<=origin with the frozen decision_date+14d proxy.
prediction_window: 12 months after each origin; training labels must mature before the next evaluation origin.
status_reason: On 2025-10-01, pair persistence AP=0.791259 versus prevalence=0.420195, company=0.570689 and track=0.506832; it is also competitive with the full model. This supports regulatory-activity persistence, not innovation or causal R&D persistence.

definition: Acceleration, measured as rd_momentum=log1p(current-12m pair events)−log1p(previous-12m pair events), provides incremental information for denser pair activity in the following 12 months.
sample_scope: Same reverse_rd_v1 continuation cohort and final three holdouts as H1; a valid test must compare otherwise identical models with and without rd_momentum.
information_cutoff: Same frozen quarterly origins and decision_date+14d proxy as H1.
prediction_window: 12 months; density is operationalised by the existing binary any-material-activity target, not a causal rate estimate.
primary_metrics: AP delta for the isolated rd_momentum feature
status_reason: rd_momentum exists only jointly with nine other shared features in the frozen comparison. No frozen leave-one-feature-out or single-momentum result isolates its effect; assigning the whole model's lift to acceleration would be invalid.

definition: An increase in active companies in a track (rd_track_active_companies_delta, current versus previous 12 months) predicts that track's overall activity growth or new company entry in the following 12 months.
sample_scope: first_entry_v1 has 41,003 matured candidate pair-origin rows, 3,833 events, 51 companies and 38 tracks. The final three holdouts have 1,722/1,721/1,716 rows and 25/27/26 positives. A track-level target would additionally be required for overall track growth.
information_cutoff: Quarterly origins 2020-01-01 through 2025-10-01; decision_date+14d proxy and unversioned current track mapping are retained as limitations.
prediction_window: 12 months; available target is first observed entry after at least 36 months of pair dormancy, not total track growth.
primary_metrics: AP delta for isolated participation-delta feature
track-level growth correlation if raw data are restored
status_reason: The participation feature is bundled with five other entry-specific features and the target is pair entry, not overall track growth. Existing results cannot identify either the isolated feature effect or the broader track-level claim.

definition: Cross-company and track-level activity features add predictive information beyond the individual company×track pair's own historical persistence.
sample_scope: Both reverse_rd_v1 continuation and first_entry_v1 entry cohorts with identical rows across each comparison; final three holdouts as H1/H3.
information_cutoff: Same frozen rolling origins and availability proxy as H1/H3.
prediction_window: 12 months for continuation and first observed entry.
primary_metrics: AP(model)−AP(pair persistence) with paired 2000-row bootstrap interval
status_reason: Continuation full-model lift over pair persistence is only +0.002218 AP with 95% CI [−0.031599,0.036774]. Entry-specific cross-company features reduce final-origin AP from 0.113927 to 0.100476, while the three-window mean changes in the opposite direction. No stable incremental value is demonstrated.

definition: Historical clinical-trial registrations provide incremental information for a later qualified FDA regulatory milestone after controlling for regulatory persistence.
sample_scope: Requires trial→company→track links with first-posted dates and independent trial/application identifiers. S-029 has 2,498 unique trials across only five firms and no matured trial-to-FDA target; reverse_rd_v1/v2 has no trial features.
information_cutoff: A valid test requires registry first-posted/update times available at each origin. Sponsor names alone or event_start dates are insufficient.
prediction_window: 12 months after origin, with trial and FDA labels matured and deduplicated across train and holdout.
status_reason: No frozen trial-to-regulatory milestone dataset exists. S-029 covers five firms and establishes major entity/time limitations but not a matured predictive target; reverse_rd_v2 does not contain trial rows. A new source may not be generated under PHOENIX constraints.

definition: For each track, company-share HHI and its change over the current versus previous 12 months explains subsequent diffusion, measured by active-company count in the next 12 months.
sample_scope: Requires the full company×track×time event panel and versioned entity/track mapping. The FDA AI paper supplies a separate 17×4 descriptive specialty cohort, not a MedRadar predictive panel.
information_cutoff: All event and mapping inputs must be available at the origin; no present-day specialty mapping may be backfilled.
prediction_window: 12 months; company participation and HHI must be computed on non-overlapping historical/future windows.
status_reason: No frozen MedRadar HHI feature or next-period diffusion target exists and the raw stores are absent. PHOENIX reproduced the external paper's descriptive HHI statistics only; that does not test concentration→diffusion.

definition: Change-point/sequential detectors outperform fixed-multiplier anomaly thresholds on company×track monthly activity after calibration to a false-alarm budget of at most 0.02.
sample_scope: detect_v1 real-data comparison: 104 cells, recent 24 months versus preceding 48 months, exact one-sided Poisson test with BH q=0.1 and 12-month post-alert novelty audit.
information_cutoff: Frozen historical monthly cells; calibration and evaluation partitions are inherited from detect_v1. No live alert is issued.
prediction_window: Alert detection followed by a descriptive 12-month novelty window, not a matured forecasting target.
status_reason: Naive multiplier and Poisson CUSUM produce zero alerts; rolling z-score produces one and Bayes factor two. All observed post-alert novelty shares are zero, so there is no positive validation basis to declare change-point methods superior.

definition: SciTrends-style lag, growth and log-momentum features transfer to medical-device event histories and provide incremental value beyond persistence and simple baselines.
sample_scope: reverse_rd_v1 and first_entry_v1 use count_12m, previous_12m, count_36m, recency and log-momentum. A valid migration test requires isolated growth-feature ablation on identical time boundaries.
information_cutoff: Same frozen rolling origins and decision_date+14d proxy. SciTrends' row-wise shared-year folds are explicitly not reused.
prediction_window: 12 months for continuation and first observed entry.
status_reason: Growth features are present and the entry model outperforms simple baselines, but no isolated SciTrends-style feature ablation exists. Continuation persistence explains 99.4% of lift over prevalence on the final origin, so transfer cannot be claimed from the joint model alone.

definition: Fusing financial, market and publication features with regulatory history outperforms the strongest single-source model on identical rows and rolling origins.
sample_scope: Ablation continuation specs A/B/C/D/E and entry specs A/B/C/D/E/F/G, all evaluated on the same final three holdouts. Procurement and patents remain excluded from predictive gain.
information_cutoff: Regulatory events use decision_date+14d; financials use filed date; publications use complete prior years with 15-Feb lag; market is day-level only.
prediction_window: 12 months for continuation and first observed entry.
status_reason: Continuation all-available E has AP=0.786696 versus regulatory-only A=0.793476 and lower three-window mean; B/C/D also fail to improve A. Entry best fusion F=0.105083 trails shared financial B=0.116347 and shared-only A=0.113927, while all-available G=0.097863. Fusion is not better in this frozen evidence, without claiming a universal negative.

definition: Complex network or lightweight machine-learning models outperform simple statistical persistence baselines on identical time boundaries.
sample_scope: Continuation and entry logistic-regression comparisons plus S-028 graph-feature study. GNNs were not run under the S-028 stopping rule; no GNN result may be inferred.
information_cutoff: Same frozen rolling origins. S-028 additionally documents estimated knowledge clocks, sparse 12.1% graph coverage and entity/mapping hindsight.
prediction_window: 12 months for the main cohorts; S-028 uses separate 2-quarter/4-quarter graph targets.
primary_metrics: AP delta with paired bootstrap interval
status_reason: Continuation logistic regression is statistically indistinguishable from pair persistence (+0.002218 AP, CI includes zero). Entry improves on the final origin but the other holdout intervals are unstable. S-028 finds no graph-improvement evidence with limited power and never runs GNNs. Neither universal superiority nor universal uselessness is established.
